2609.27510.title: Uncheatable Eval: Dynamic Compression-Based Evaluation of Language Models
2609.27510.paper_summary: Modern large language models are pretrained on massive datasets, making it difficult to prevent benchmark data from entering their training sets and undermining the reliability of evaluation results. Reliable evaluation is particularly challenging for base models, whose limited instruction-following ability complicates task-based assessment. We introduce Uncheatable Eval, a dynamic benchmark that regularly collects newly published text to evaluate base language models and reduce the risk of data contamination. Drawing on the relationship between a model's predictive ability and its ability to compress data losslessly, we use compression rate to evaluate how well models predict new text. We evaluate 80 models across 14 text categories, study how compression changes with context length, and examine the correlation between compression rate and zero-shot MMLU accuracy. Our results yield three main findings: (1) compression performance follows a consistent scaling trend with model size; (2) attention-based, hybrid, and recurrent models differ in how their compression performance changes as more context becomes available; and (3) lower compression rates are strongly associated with higher zero-shot MMLU accuracy. Code is available at https://github.com/Jellyfish042/uncheatable_eval.
2609.27510.paper_summary_zh: 現代大型語言模型在龐大的數據集上進行預訓練，這使得防止基準數據進入其訓練集並削弱評估結果的可靠性變得困難。對於基礎模型而言，可靠的評估尤其具有挑戰性，因為其有限的指令跟隨能力使得基於任務的評估變得複雜。我們介紹了Uncheatable Eval，一個動態基準，定期收集新發表的文本以評估基礎語言模型並降低數據污染的風險。根據模型的預測能力與其無損壓縮數據的能力之間的關係，我們使用壓縮率來評估模型預測新文本的能力。我們在14個文本類別中評估了80個模型，研究了隨著上下文長度變化的壓縮情況，並檢查了壓縮率與零-shot MMLU 準確性之間的相關性。我們的結果得出了三個主要發現：（1）壓縮性能隨著模型大小遵循一致的擴展趨勢；（2）基於注意力的、混合的和循環模型在可用上下文增多時其壓縮性能的變化有所不同；（3）較低的壓縮率與較高的零-shot MMLU 準確性之間有強烈的相關性。代碼可在 https://github.com/Jellyfish042/uncheatable_eval 獲得。
